pr_title: executor: optimize (left outer) (anti) semi join which has no other condition
pr_body:

PR Title Format:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/47424

Problem Summary:
The sql will be very slow if there are a lot of matched row for each row from build side in (left outer) (anti) semi join.

### What is changed and how it works?
Recognize this case then optimize it.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No need to test
  > - [ ] I checked and no code files have been changed.
  > <!-- Or your custom  "No need to test" reasons -->  

Before
```
mysql> select count(*) from customer a where exists (select 1 from customer b where a.C_NATIONKEY=b.C_NATIONKEY);
+----------+
| count(*) |
+----------+
|   150000 |
+----------+
1 row in set (36.32 sec)
```
After
```
mysql> select count(*) from customer a where exists (select 1 from customer b where a.C_NATIONKEY=b.C_NATIONKEY);
+----------+
| count(*) |
+----------+
|   150000 |
+----------+
1 row in set (0.16 sec)
```

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

### Release note


issue_context.title: execution: semi join takes too long to run
comments: This is hardly a bug. I'm removing the bug label. But we are looking into why semi join is unexpectedly slow.

review_comments: Will it be better to add a comment example here for how to iterator the stored ptrs?
Is this optimazation works for nullaware join? And since only `joinMatchedProbeSideRow2Chunk` is check `isSemiJoinWithoutCondition`, nullaware join is not optimized even if it return `true` here.
No. This function is useless for null-aware semi join.
